events.description: A link in a forum thread about a food token leads to a chat server of a few thousand anonymous farmers awake in every time zone. They answer his questions at three in the morning and call him Kez after his wallet name. It is the first band that has needed him since the guild.

events.description: Kieran farms through the night, answers newcomers in the Sharehouse at three in the morning, watches six thousand pounds become thirty-eight and then seventy-one thousand on the screen, builds the Hart's crypto-payment block by day and pays his parents' rent after the plant closes.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.boundary: Kieran's state in early January 2022, before the deposit moves.
events.description: The market is a third down from November; his seventy-one thousand is forty-five on the screen. House prices in Wroughton have risen faster than their deposit. His father has been out of work since July and pretends not to mind. The Sharehouse has spent December saying that the smart money is in safe yield now, twenty percent in a dollar that does not move. He believes he understands risk; what he feels is the old fear of being left behind and the new want to provide. He has not told Laura how much he has made or lost.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.description: Four months out of the second wave and still sleeping badly. She wants to buy a house by the summer and has saved most of the deposit from overtime. She has not opened their savings app since the spring: Kieran is the one who knows about money, the way the monitors know about the patient. She is tired of being the one who holds everything.

events.description: Four nights at the spare-room desk with the Sharehouse open on one screen and the price on the other. He reads the mechanism again and understands exactly why a run feeds itself. He does not sell at ninety cents, or sixty, or twenty. Laura is on nights; the rota says so. By Friday the deposit is worth about three thousand pounds and falling.

events.boundary: Mid-June 2022: five weeks of hiding, then the mortgage forces it.
events.description: For five weeks Kieran goes to work and comes home and says nothing; he takes scam calls in the day and checks a dead balance at night. When the mortgage adviser emails for statements, Laura forwards it to him with a thumbs-up. He tells her that evening at the kitchen table, the rota on the fridge behind her.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.boundary: Summer 2022: Laura stays and holds it together in silence.
events.description: She listens, asks three practical questions, and goes to bed. In the morning she moves their accounts into her name, picks up two extra shifts a week and cancels the mortgage appointment. She does not shout and does not cry in front of him. The conversation that should happen does not happen. The rota stays on the fridge.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.boundary: August 2022: Barbara goes to Laura herself.
events.description: Something none of the named options held (the remainder was drawn). Barbara, who has never met Laura, takes the bus into Swindon on a weekday while Kieran is at the Hart and knocks on the Wood Street flat. She says who she is. She tells Laura what she did: she gave him a key without a map, and in February she knew how the peg could fail and said nothing, because she has never been anybody's mother. That part is hers, she says; the rest is his; and Laura is allowed to say something. For the first time since June, Laura does.
provenance: rabbit-hole-run; authored by the calling LLM under the human's delegation
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.boundary: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been anybody's mother and does not mean to start.

events.boundary: Monday 21 October 2019, 3.40 pm: Kieran's scam-check call to Barbara.
events.description: He reads the script: has anyone contacted you and asked you to move your money, have you been promised returns. She laughs, answers every question and then asks hers: how old is the system he works in, and who could switch it off? He finds he does not know. She asks his name. The payment is released at 4.55.

events.boundary: Evening of 12 March 2020: Kieran types the twelve words in.
events.description: At the kitchen table in the flat, with the news on about the crash, he downloads a wallet app, types the words, and presses his thumb to the glass to confirm. The balance rises: 0.0071 bitcoin, about twenty-eight pounds. Then he finds the public ledger and the transaction that sent it to him, and every transaction before it since 2009.

events.boundary: September 2022 onward: they stay and rebuild in the open.
events.description: They open one joint account that both can see, put the rota and a spreadsheet on the fridge side by side, and postpone the house by two years. Kieran deletes the trading apps and tells Laura every number. Laura, who has never asked for anything, asks for Sundays off together and gets them. Rebuilding is slow and dull and they choose it.

events.boundary: Autumn 2022 to March 2023: Kieran stays at his desk by choice, with open eyes.
events.description: He stays on the payments-exceptions desk at the Hart. The routine is the same and he is not: he knows how old the machine is and what runs under it, he knows what the new machine did to him, and he keeps Barbara's card with its small balance behind his bus pass. When a flagged transfer to a crypto exchange comes up he makes the call, reads the script, and then asks his own questions. He walks with Barbara once a month, and in March 2023 Laura comes too.
